L161: This release closes several security issues in the Agent TARS CLI server (`@agent-tars/cli`, `@tarko/agent-server`). It changes how the server can be reached, so please read Upgrading from 0.3.0 before you update.
L162: ## Upgrading from 0.3.0
L163: 
L164: If you run the CLI on your own machine and open it at `http://localhost`, nothing changes.
L165: 
L166: Otherwise:
L167:   * The server only listens on `127.0.0.1` by default. It used to listen on all network interfaces. To reach it from another machine or from outside a container, pass `--host`, e.g. `--host 0.0.0.0`.
L168:   * A non-loopback `--host` requires an access token. Set one with `--auth-token` or `TARKO_AUTH_TOKEN` (at least 16 characters). If you set none, a random token is generated on every start and printed with a ready-to-open `?token=` link, so old links stop working after a restart. Set a fixed token if you need stable links.
L169:   * Domains, reverse proxies and port forwarding need `TARKO_ALLOWED_HOSTS`. Requests whose `Host` header is not a loopback name, an IP address or the configured `--host` are rejected with `403 Invalid Host header`. Add your hostname, comma-separated: `TARKO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=agent.example.com`.
L170:   * A Web UI served from a non-localhost origin needs `TARKO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS`. Otherwise creating a session fails with `403 Origin not allowed`. Use the full origin: `TARKO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://agent.example.com`.
L171:   * `agentOptions` from requests and URLs only accepts `agentMode`. This applies to `/creating?agentOptions=...`, welcome cards and `POST /api/v1/sessions/create`. Any other key (`mcpServers`, `model`, `aioSandbox`, ...) is rejected with `400`. Configure those on the server instead.
L172:   * Direct API calls need a CSRF token. Fetch one from `GET /api/v1/csrf-token` and send it as the `x-csrf-token` header on `POST` requests. When the server requires an access token, also send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
L173: Example for a remote server behind a domain:
L174: 
L175:     TARKO_AUTH_TOKEN=<a long random string> \
L176:     TARKO_ALLOWED_HOSTS=agent.example.com \
L177:     TARKO_ALLOWED_ORIGINS=https://agent.example.com \
L178:     agent-tars --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8888
L179: 
L180: See the cite77†CLI docs†agent-tars.com for details.
L181: ## Security
L182: 
L183:   * Block request-body injection into agent constructor options; the server now binds to `127.0.0.1` by default (cite78†#1939 )
L184:   * Require an access token once the server leaves loopback (cite79†#2026 )
L185:   * Validate the `Host` header to prevent DNS rebinding (cite80†#1975 )
L186:   * Add CSRF protection, a CORS allowlist and security headers (cite81†#1853 )
L187:   * Stop HTML previews from escaping their iframe sandbox (cite82†#1938 )
L188: ## Bug Fixes
L189: 
L190:   * Answer a disallowed origin with 403 instead of 500 (cite83†#2044 )
L191:   * Repair unterminated strings in truncated tool call JSON (cite84†#1836 )
L192:   * Handle unknown model providers by defaulting to OpenAI-compatible (cite85†#1823 )
L193:   * Support streaming usage on LLM responses (cite86†#1737 )
L194: ## Features

L196:   * Add embed-frame support for nav items (cite87†#1761 )
L197:   * Optimize the session status action design (cite88†#1766 )
L198:   * Set the remote browser viewport to the default viewport (cite89†#1748 )
L199:   * Add `@gui-agent/cli`, a CLI for GUI Agent automation (cite90†#1741 )

L0: # MCP protocol and skills
L1: 
L2: The Rust `cua-driver mcp` endpoint supports modern MCP `2026-07-28` over stdio
L3: and retains the legacy `initialize` flow with version `2025-06-18`. Direct and
L4: daemon-backed stdio use the same protocol and skill catalog.
L5: This implementation shipped in Cua Driver 0.28.0 through PR #3609. MCP uses
L6: date-based protocol revisions: `2026-07-28` is the modern revision implemented
L7: here. The JSON-RPC `2.0` envelope and MCP SDK 2.x package versions are separate
L8: version numbers, so “MCP 2.0” is not a precise protocol revision name.
L9: ## Connect
L10: 
L11: Keep the existing MCP server command:
L12: 
L13: ```json
L14: {
L15:   "command": "cua-driver",
L16:   "args": ["mcp"]
L17: }
L18: ```
L19: 
L20: A modern client sends protocol metadata on every request. Discovery does not
L21: require initialization:
L22: 
L23: ```json
L24: {
L25:   "jsonrpc": "2.0",
L26:   "id": 1,
L27:   "method": "server/discover",
L28:   "params": {
L29:     "_meta": {
L30:       "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28",
L31:       "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": {}
L32:     }
L33:   }
L34: }
L35: ```
L36: The response reports the supported modern version, tools, resources, and the
L37: `io.modelcontextprotocol/skills` extension. Every modern result includes
L38: `resultType: "complete"`. Discovery and list/read responses include conservative
L39: cache hints. Capabilities are per request; successful discovery does not excuse
L40: missing metadata on subsequent requests.
L41: Legacy clients negotiate `2025-06-18` through
L42: `initialize.params.protocolVersion`, then make metadata-free requests. The
L43: namespaced `io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion` key is modern-only; using
L44: it with `2025-06-18` is rejected as an unsupported per-request version.
L45: Protocol metadata never grants desktop permissions, changes the runtime mode,
L46: or transfers another connection's session ownership. Repeat explicit Driver
L47: session names on calls as usual. When a response is lost, verify state before
L48: retrying an action.
L49: ## Read the bundled skill
L50: 
L51: Use `skills/list` to discover the catalog. Use `skills/get` with
L52: `uri: "skill://cua-driver/SKILL.md"` to retrieve the skill entry, including its
L53: full frontmatter and resource manifest. The entry lists every bundled file,
L54: with a `sha256:` digest and byte size.
L55: 
L56: Use `resources/read` to fetch a listed URI. For example, a modern request is:
L57: ```json
L58: {
L59:   "jsonrpc": "2.0",
L60:   "id": 2,
L61:   "method": "resources/read",
L62:   "params": {
L63:     "uri": "skill://cua-driver/SKILL.md",
L64:     "_meta": {
L65:       "io.modelcontextprotocol/protocolVersion": "2026-07-28",
L66:       "io.modelcontextprotocol/clientCapabilities": {
L67:         "extensions": { "io.modelcontextprotocol/skills": {} }
L68:       }
L69:     }
L70:   }
L71: }
L72: ```
L73: The eight-file pack includes the main skill, README, platform guides, browser
L74: guide, recording guide, and embedding guide. It is embedded in the endpoint
L75: binary, so serving it needs no separate skill installation. Only those exact
L76: resource URIs are readable. Directory listing, archives, arbitrary local
L77: files, and script execution are not supported by this endpoint.
L78: Clients verify each resource's raw UTF-8 bytes against the manifest before
L79: using it. Reading a resource does not activate a skill. The host owns skill
L80: selection, content-bound consent, and any execution approval. A base MCP client
L81: may support tools and resource reads without supporting native skill loading.
L82: ## Verified client behavior
L83: 
L84: A clean macOS VM test with the released Cua Driver 0.28.0 established these
L85: client boundaries:
L86: - Codex 0.154.0 discovered and read the embedded skill through its MCP resource
L87:   APIs with the filesystem skill link absent, then used the Driver tools.
L88: - Claude Code 2.1.268 listed and read the embedded resources explicitly with
L89:   the filesystem skill link absent. It did not include the remote skill in its
L90:   native startup skill catalog, so filesystem installation remains the native
L91:   activation path for that client version.
L92: Both clients completed a background Calculator action while another app stayed
L93: active. Those runs verify client interoperability and resource access. They do
L94: not change the host-owned activation, consent, or action-approval boundaries.
L95: 
L96: The Skills extension follows accepted SEP-2640 at
L97: `d6b31a03504c15677d49b922b6b6ace0ef65728d`; its upstream publication is still
L98: pending. In particular, cache metadata for `skills/get` is unresolved upstream,
L99: so Driver does not add cache hints to that method.
L100: ## HTTP limitation
L101: 
L102: The authenticated loopback HTTP endpoint remains on legacy MCP. It explicitly
L103: rejects modern metadata and discovery requests. Use stdio for `2026-07-28`.
L104: Modern HTTP requires a reviewed application-handle contract so sessions can
L105: survive connection changes without weakening client isolation. OAuth and
L106: gateway ownership remain in RFC #3197.
L107: ## Reproduce the protocol check
L108: 
L109: From the repository root, install the isolated test dependencies and point the
L110: probe at the source-built candidate:
L111: 
L112: ```sh
L113: npm ci --ignore-scripts --prefix .github/scripts/cua-driver-mcp-compat/modern-client
L114: CUA_DRIVER_BINARY=/absolute/path/to/cua-driver \
L115:   node .github/scripts/cua-driver-mcp-compat/verify-modern.mjs
L116: ```
L117: The probe uses `@modelcontextprotocol/client` 2.0.0 with the modern version
L118: pinned. It verifies discovery, a read-only tool call, skill enumeration and
L119: retrieval, complete resource bytes and hashes, and invalid-request rejection.
L120: It uses isolated state and makes no model or account calls. CI runs this probe
L121: on Linux, macOS, and Windows. This proves server/SDK interoperability, not
L122: native skill activation in a particular host.

L25: ## Session lifecycle
L26: 
L27: For multi-call work, prefer a short public label and pass the same label on every call that accepts it. Passing it once is not sticky: omission uses the transport's implicit session. Named CLI state is shared only within the daemon's CLI namespace, not with arbitrary MCP connections or a new daemon generation.
L28: `start_session` is optional: actions can establish the run. Use it to configure the initial cursor theme or revive a name after `end_session`. The default idle TTL is five minutes; do not assume a long human permission wait preserves handles.
L29: 
L30: ```bash
L31: cua-driver start_session '{"session":"run-1"}'
L32: # Discover, observe, act, and verify; repeat session:"run-1".
L33: cua-driver end_session '{"session":"run-1"}'
L34: ```
L35: Explicit targets own observation/input modality, not session configuration. There is no `deescalate_session`. Do not use retired `capture_scope` settings or legacy escalation-session tools in new workflows. Reserved fields such as `_session_id` belong to the transport, never to an agent.

L37: ## Foreground boundary
L38: 
L39: `delivery_mode:"foreground"` is a user-visible takeover boundary, not an automatic retry. Use it only when the user already authorized visible control for this workflow or after asking. It can change focus, workspace, or the physical cursor; restoration is best-effort and adapter-dependent.
L40: If foreground control is not authorized, stop with the driver's refusal instead of silently escalating. Refresh state and do not retry automatically. An authorized desktop target intentionally uses system input, but it still requires the exact display resource to be admitted. A failed window capture is not desktop permission.
L41: Use Cua's tools rather than shell activation/input shims. `bring_to_front` is reserved for requested persistent foreground state or a focus-proxy surface that must remain active across calls. A native menu operation can also activate temporarily; prefer an in-window control when background posture matters.
L42: ## Keep authorization separate from sessions
L43: 
L44: This section is about Cua Driver's authorization profile. It is separate from the macOS privacy approvals (TCC) that the app itself needs; see [MACOS.md](MACOS.md#install-and-approve-permissions).
L45: The trusted host selects one permission profile at startup. `standard` keeps
L46: the normal profile behavior and residual approval requirements, `bounded`
L47: requires a reviewed capability manifest and has no runtime approval path, and
L48: `unrestricted` bypasses Cua approval prompts after explicit risk acceptance.
L49: Hard invariants plus managed and user policy remain binding in every profile.
L50: An optional capability manifest is a deny-by-default ceiling in `standard` and
L51: `unrestricted`; `bounded` requires one. It can remove tools or typed resources
L52: from the selected profile, but it cannot grant a tool, resource, or approval
L53: bypass that another authorization layer denies. Approval is considered only
L54: after the tool and every adapter-attested resource are inside manifest scope.
